page: Google Cloud Platform a4-highgpu-8g is an accelerator-optimized server belonging to the a4 family. It features 224 dedicated vCPUs built on the x86_64 architecture. The system is equipped with 3968.0 GB of system memory, providing approximately 17.71 GB of RAM per core.

This server integrates eight NVIDIA B200 GPUs from the Blackwell family, delivering a total of 1440 GB of VRAM. For local storage, the configuration includes 12885 GB of local NVMe SSD capacity. It does not include any complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Given the high-density hardware profile, this server represents a specialized tier of resource allocation. The integration of massive GPU memory, high-capacity local NVMe SSDs, and extensive system RAM positions it in a premium hardware class. Tradeoffs include the lack of complimentary public IPv4 addresses and the high resource commitment required for deployment.

The hardware configuration is designed for workloads requiring massive parallel processing and large memory footprints. Appropriate use cases include large-scale machine learning model training, complex data science jobs, large-scale LLM inference, and database workloads that leverage GPU acceleration and high-speed local NVMe storage.
